title: CrossOver Mac user guide
observation: CodeWeavers says a bottle contains a Windows registry, CrossOver settings, applications, and saved user data. The guide separates application uninstall, irreversible bottle deletion, bottle archive and restore, and installer-cache clearing.
product_implication: Model a CrossOver bottle as a mixed dependency group. Offer archive before deletion and keep installer cache separate from saved data.
quality_note: Current first-party CrossOver Mac guide. It defines owner behavior but does not measure user frequency.

title: Archiving and restoring a CrossOver bottle
observation: CodeWeavers documents owner actions that export a bottle to a cxarchive file and restore that archive as a bottle.
product_implication: Treat a verified cxarchive as a recovery artifact and test owner import before recommending source-bottle removal.
quality_note: First-party procedural documentation with explicit archive and restore steps.

title: Using the CrossOver removal tool
observation: CodeWeavers says its removal tool deletes CrossOver, installed Windows applications, and CrossOver files. It tells users to archive bottles first if they want to keep installed applications.
product_implication: Do not present a full CrossOver removal as routine cache cleanup. Require an archive or an explicit no-recovery choice.
quality_note: First-party removal guide with a direct data-loss warning.

title: Add CrossOver bottles outside the default folder
observation: CodeWeavers documents moving a whole bottle to another location and leaving a symbolic link where CrossOver expects it. The article calls out large game installs on external drives.
product_implication: Record the symlink and target volume as required owner state. A missing target is unavailable storage, not an abandoned bottle.
quality_note: First-party path and registration procedure for external bottle storage.

title: Browsing external volumes from CrossOver applications
observation: CodeWeavers maps the home folder, system root, external volumes, and bottle C drive into different Windows drive views.
product_implication: Resolve save and payload paths through the active drive mapping. A Windows path alone is not enough to identify the physical volume.
quality_note: First-party documentation for CrossOver drive mappings.

title: Heroic save path and cloud-sync resolution
observation: Heroic resolves Epic and GOG save locations from install metadata, platform variables, and Wine prefix state. The source contains explicit failure paths when save or install paths are missing.
product_implication: Require a resolved local save path and owner metadata before declaring cloud protection or deleting a prefix.
quality_note: First-party source pinned to commit 37a9bef. Source behavior can change in later commits.

title: Heroic prefix and settings removal logic
observation: Heroic removes a prefix recursively only after path checks, and it can separately remove game settings and logs. Shared and default prefix paths are protected from automatic removal.
product_implication: Mirror the owner's path guards. Show prefix, settings, and logs as separate effects rather than one cleanup size.
quality_note: First-party source pinned to commit 37a9bef.

title: Heroic uninstall confirmation model
observation: Heroic warns that prefix removal cannot be undone and removes saves that lack backup. It presents settings and log erasure as a separate option and blocks uninstall while a game is running.
product_implication: Use the same separation and add recovery proof. Do not reduce the warning to a generic delete confirmation.
quality_note: First-party source pinned to commit 37a9bef with user-facing warning text.

title: Legendary uninstall keep-files option
observation: Heroic's Legendary uninstall command supports a keep-files option, which separates launcher registration removal from game-file removal.
product_implication: Offer owner deregistration without payload deletion when the owner supports it. Report the two effects separately.
quality_note: Small first-party command schema pinned to commit 37a9bef.

title: Prism instance copy categories
observation: Prism represents saves, playtime, options, resource packs, shader packs, servers, mods, configs, and screenshots as separate copy choices.
product_implication: Use these owner categories when showing what an instance move or archive preserves. Do not call the whole instance replaceable.
quality_note: First-party source pinned to Prism commit 33996a2.

title: Prism staged instance copy task
observation: Prism can copy, link, hardlink, or clone an instance into a staging path. It has a special path that copies saves instead of linking them and reports copy failure or abort.
product_implication: Measure exclusive reclaimed bytes across links and clones. Keep source data until the staged copy and a launch test succeed.
quality_note: First-party source pinned to Prism commit 33996a2.

title: ATLauncher instance export choices
observation: ATLauncher lets users select an export location and choose instance folders. Its export logic treats mods, configs, resource packs, and shader packs as named content groups and excludes launcher-specific files.
product_implication: Show the export manifest and exclusions. A successful archive file alone does not prove that every personal folder was included.
quality_note: First-party source pinned to ATLauncher commit 9e6aa14.

title: ATLauncher backup modes and destination
observation: ATLauncher offers backups for saves, configs, and options, an expanded mode that includes mods, and a full-instance mode. Users can choose the backup folder and enable backup after launch.
product_implication: Record backup mode, destination, completion time, and included groups before using a backup as deletion proof.
quality_note: First-party source pinned to ATLauncher commit 9e6aa14.

title: itch owner uninstall operation
observation: The itch app sends a cave identifier to its owner uninstall operation and tracks the task through owner messages instead of deleting an arbitrary folder directly.
product_implication: Use the owner's cave identifier and uninstall action. Verify both owner state and remaining files after completion.
quality_note: First-party source pinned to itch commit c64c917.

title: itch install-location removal guards
observation: The itch app refuses to remove the last install location and asks for confirmation before removing another registered path.
product_implication: Treat install-location removal as owner metadata mutation. Do not infer that games inside the path should also be deleted.
quality_note: First-party source pinned to itch commit c64c917.

title: PlayCover uninstall effects
observation: PlayCover exposes separate uninstall effects for app data, keymaps, settings, entitlements, and PlayChain state before deleting the app and its alias.
product_implication: Show each effect and its path or identifier. App removal does not imply that all associated state was removed.
quality_note: First-party source pinned to PlayCover commit 4916e6a.

title: PlayCover uninstall defaults
observation: PlayCover stores separate default switches for clearing app data, keymaps, settings, entitlements, and PlayChain state. Those destructive switches default to false in this commit.
product_implication: Read owner defaults at action time and never assume associated data will be removed with the app.
quality_note: First-party source pinned to PlayCover commit 4916e6a.

title: Legendary cannot find installed games
observation: A Heroic user reported that Legendary could no longer launch games that Heroic still presented after an update.
product_implication: A visible library entry does not prove a working owner record. Run the launcher and game after any registration repair.
quality_note: Direct owner issue with logs. Platform behavior may differ from macOS.

title: Downloaded Witcher update remained stuck during install
observation: A user reported an update that had downloaded but repeatedly stalled during installation despite about 500 GB free.
product_implication: Separate downloaded bytes, unpacked staging, install progress, and free space. A large free-space value does not make partial files safe to remove while owner work is active.
quality_note: Direct report with a counterexample to simple free-space diagnosis.

title: Heroic forced new games into one shared prefix
observation: A user reported that new games were forced into a shared prefix and Heroic would not retain separate-prefix choices.
product_implication: Detect shared prefixes before calculating per-game reclaim. One prefix may own several games and their saves.
quality_note: Direct report. It shows a shared-state failure, not its prevalence.

title: Artwork selection reset prefix and executable choices
observation: A user reported that opening the artwork picker reset the chosen prefix, Wine version, executable path, and shared-prefix setting.
product_implication: Snapshot owner configuration before edits and re-read it afterward. Cosmetic owner actions can alter launch-critical state.
quality_note: Direct owner issue with a reproducible metadata-loss path.

title: Heroic failed when the Games folder was a symlink
observation: A user moved Heroic storage through a symlink, but Heroic kept recreating its default path and failed to launch.
product_implication: Do not prescribe a symlink as a generic move strategy. Verify owner support and launch after remount.
quality_note: Direct owner issue on Linux. The path dependency is adjacent to macOS external storage.

title: Heroic user requested a portable game backup
observation: A user asked Heroic for an owner-generated backup because manual game backup was tedious and physical media was unavailable.
product_implication: Distinguish a verified owner backup from a copied install folder. Show whether the backup can reinstall offline.
quality_note: Direct feature request. It captures a recovery need, not existing behavior.

title: Cancelled update left repeated processes and a stuck game
observation: A user reported that cancelling and restarting an update spawned repeated processes and left the update at zero percent even after cache and install-file cleanup.
product_implication: Block cleanup while owner processes or locks remain. A failed owner update needs a recovery path before staging deletion.
quality_note: Direct report across two games with the same observed result.

title: Reinstalled Heroic could not rediscover imported games
observation: A user described having to re-import every game after reinstalling Heroic even though the game folders had not changed.
product_implication: Treat missing owner registration as recoverable metadata. Offer owner rescan or import before redownload or deletion.
quality_note: Direct feature request with a concrete reinstall workflow.

title: Heroic uninstall removed non-native files and saves
observation: A user reported that uninstall removed a whole game directory containing saves, portraits, modules, and scripts that Heroic had not installed.
product_implication: Inventory foreign and personal files inside an install root before owner uninstall. Require backup or explicit exclusion when the owner may remove the whole directory.
quality_note: Direct data-loss report with named personal content.

title: Sideloaded games shared one Heroic prefix
observation: A user reported that every sideloaded game was assigned to one prefix named sideload instead of separate game prefixes.
product_implication: Trace all games that reference a prefix before deletion. Per-game selection cannot safely delete a shared prefix.
quality_note: Direct owner issue with a reproducible shared-prefix state.

title: Heroic cloud save sync failed with invalid owner metadata
observation: A user saw cloud sync disabled because the expected Epic manifest path was invalid, while the tool reported no remote saves.
product_implication: Do not equate zero remote saves with safe local deletion. Show the sync error and keep local saves protected.
quality_note: Direct report with owner log output.

title: Run Installer First overwrote a prefix path
observation: A user reported that running an installer inside an existing game changed the saved prefix path to an invalid placeholder.
product_implication: Preserve and compare prefix metadata around owner installer actions. A missing path can hide live container data.
quality_note: Direct owner issue with the altered path state.

title: Offline mode remained enabled for unsupported games
observation: Heroic maintainers described repeated support cases where offline mode was enabled for games that did not support it and users did not know the setting was active.
product_implication: Test offline launch per game. A local payload does not prove the game can run without owner authentication.
quality_note: Owner issue grounded in support cases. It does not quantify incidence.

title: Invalid cached install info discarded a completed download
observation: A user reported that an empty folder name in cached install metadata caused Heroic to download a game and then lose the downloaded content at the end. Clearing the metadata cache fixed the next install.
product_implication: Classify metadata cache by effect. Some cache repair is safe, but partial payload should remain until owner retry or inspection.
quality_note: Direct report with owner logs and a successful counter-test.

title: Epic cloud save download had no chunks
observation: A user could not force-download cloud saves because the owner tool found no available chunks and requested a clean-saves repair.
product_implication: Treat cloud repair as unresolved until a save loads in game. Keep local saves and record both generations.
quality_note: Direct first-person report with the exact owner error.

title: Imported games received a shared default prefix
observation: A user found that imported games used the parent default prefix while newly installed games used separate child prefixes.
product_implication: Do not infer prefix ownership from the install folder. Read each imported game's actual owner setting and shared references.
quality_note: Direct report comparing imported and newly installed behavior.

title: Cloud sync mixed saves with machine-specific settings
observation: A user reported that one cloud location held both saves and a resolution file, forcing configuration changes after switching devices.
product_implication: Show the cloud file set, not only a sync badge. Machine-specific config can make cloud state unsuitable as a full restore.
quality_note: Direct cross-device counterexample.

title: Heroic silently skipped save download without a path
observation: The owner issue states that auto sync could appear enabled while save download failed because no local save path was set, with the error visible only in logs.
product_implication: Require a resolved local path and successful sync receipt before showing cloud-protected status.
quality_note: Owner issue with a defined failure condition and logs.

title: Uninstall removed prefixes after game files were already gone
observation: A user manually deleted game files, then used Heroic uninstall because the stale library entry remained. The owner action also removed prefixes.
product_implication: When payload is already missing, default to deregistration only. Protect any remaining prefix until its saves are inventoried.
quality_note: Direct report connecting stale registration to secondary prefix loss.

title: User deleted prefix saves through a tired uninstall choice
observation: A user said they accidentally left prefix removal selected during late-night troubleshooting and lost saves that were not backed up.
product_implication: Use a separate confirmation that names the save path and backup state. Do not rely on a nearby checkbox note.
quality_note: Direct first-person data-loss report and request for a stronger warning.

title: Prism export retained an instance UUID
observation: A user reported that Prism exported and re-imported the same instance UUID, which could preserve identity where a new imported instance was expected.
product_implication: Verify owner identity after restore. A copied archive can collide with the source instance or its metadata.
quality_note: Direct owner issue with a specific identity field.

title: Locked disabled mod caused endless duplicate files
observation: A locked disabled mod triggered Prism to create duplicate-numbered copies repeatedly instead of completing a rename.
product_implication: Detect active locks and repeating siblings before cleanup. Stop the owner process before offering duplicate removal.
quality_note: Direct report with a reproducible disk-growth loop.

title: Prism user wanted automatic backups before mod updates
observation: A modded Minecraft player requested a full instance copy before bulk mod updates because updates had repeatedly broken the instance.
product_implication: Offer owner backup before reclaiming old mods or configs, and keep the backup until a post-update launch succeeds.
quality_note: Direct feature request based on repeated personal recovery work.

title: Prism could not import an exported mod list
observation: A user could export a mod list but could not import it into another instance, so the list was not a restore artifact.
product_implication: Do not count a list as a backup. Require a tested owner import or reproducible package sources.
quality_note: Direct feature request that exposes an export-only counterexample.

title: Downloaded modpacks failed to launch offline
observation: A user reported that previously installed modpacks still attempted a Mojang metadata download and failed offline.
product_implication: Test launch with networking disabled before classifying a modded instance as offline-ready.
quality_note: Direct owner issue with a named failing dependency request.

title: Prism CLI offline launch still required Microsoft auth
observation: A user found that Prism's offline command-line launch still blocked on Microsoft authentication when Wi-Fi was disabled.
product_implication: An offline flag is not proof. Record the exact launch path and a successful network-disabled run.
quality_note: Direct owner issue with reproducible CLI steps.

title: Resource-pack list had no import counterpart
observation: A player asked for resource-pack list export like the mod list so they could share and rebuild the set.
product_implication: Protect resource packs unless the exact files or an owner-restorable manifest exists.
quality_note: Direct feature request. It identifies a missing recovery mechanism.

title: Prism account disappeared after an update
observation: A user reported that updating Prism removed the saved account and forced a new login.
product_implication: Keep account and token loss separate from game-data loss. Verify that restored instances can still authenticate or launch offline.
quality_note: Direct report with limited cause evidence.

title: Prism renamed an instance folder while Minecraft was running
observation: A macOS user renamed an instance and its folder while Minecraft was running, with no warning.
product_implication: Check open files and running processes before move or cleanup. Require a clean owner shutdown first.
quality_note: Direct macOS issue with simple reproduction steps.

title: Prism import failed when its host was unreachable
observation: A user could not install an imported pack because a required host was unreachable.
product_implication: Mark remote dependencies and test them before deleting local mods. An import manifest may not be reproducible later.
quality_note: Direct owner issue. Host failure is specific, but the recovery dependency is general.

title: Repacked Modrinth export was not recognized
observation: A user unzipped and repacked a Modrinth export, after which Prism no longer recognized it.
product_implication: Validate archive structure through owner import. File presence and a zip extension do not prove recoverability.
quality_note: Direct owner issue with a clear archive counterexample.

title: Offline and online sessions conflicted on macOS
observation: A macOS user could not join a LAN session when one device used the same Microsoft account offline and another used it online.
product_implication: A post-move test must cover the user's real account mode. Starting the game alone does not prove session recovery.
quality_note: Direct macOS issue with cross-device reproduction.

title: Prism offline control still depended on auth
observation: A user said Launch Offline still authenticated when online and failed during an authentication outage, making the control unreliable.
product_implication: Show observed offline readiness, not the presence of an owner button.
quality_note: Direct report and design request based on actual outage behavior.

title: Launch Offline hung on an unavailable auth service
observation: A user could not start single-player offline because Prism still tried to contact an unavailable Mojang service.
product_implication: Preserve local runtime and metadata until a network-disabled launch completes.
quality_note: Direct owner issue filed during an authentication outage.

title: Partial API outage blocked an existing offline account
observation: A user reported that one failing Microsoft API prevented offline launch even though the account already existed locally.
product_implication: Test partial network failure as well as full disconnection. Offline recovery can fail in both states.
quality_note: Direct owner issue with the partial-outage condition.

title: Offline instance still tried to update asset index
observation: A user reported that an offline account still triggered online asset-index work and failed to launch.
product_implication: Include asset indexes and runtime metadata in offline-readiness checks. They are not disposable merely because assets can usually redownload.
quality_note: Direct owner issue from a user who depended on offline accounts.

title: Authentication failure removed the saved Prism profile
observation: A user reported that a failed reauthentication removed the local Prism account and then prevented offline play.
product_implication: Back up owner account metadata before repair. Do not clean it as stale merely because remote authentication failed.
quality_note: Direct data-loss report during a service outage.

title: Cross-platform Prism import lost file permissions
observation: An instance exported on Windows and imported on Linux had files with unusable permissions until the user repaired them manually.
product_implication: A restore test must include permissions and launch, not only archive extraction.
quality_note: Direct cross-platform issue with reproducible steps.

title: Removing mods left old configuration files
observation: A player wanted Prism to remove configs that remained after the related mods were deleted.
product_implication: Old config can be clutter, but ownership is uncertain. Show the former mod link and keep user-edited config out of automatic deletion.
quality_note: Direct feature request. It does not prove every leftover config is safe.

title: Pack world did not restore into the saves folder
observation: A user reported that a world bundled with a modpack remained zipped instead of becoming a playable save after install.
product_implication: Test world visibility and open the world after restore. A world archive inside the instance is not equivalent to a restored save.
quality_note: Direct report across more than one modpack.

title: ATLauncher update check prevented offline play
observation: A user reported that ATLauncher's failed update checks stopped Minecraft when the computer had no internet connection.
product_implication: Test owner startup and game launch offline. Installed payload alone is insufficient.
quality_note: Direct report with the failing owner request in logs.

title: Deleting disabledmods broke mod controls
observation: A user deleted the disabledmods folder while preparing a pack and then could no longer disable mods because the owner operation expected that folder.
product_implication: Do not classify an empty owner folder as disposable without checking whether the launcher recreates it.
quality_note: Direct report with a manual-cleanup counterexample.

title: ATLauncher crashed when run from external USB storage
observation: A user launched the ATLauncher jar from an external USB device and it crashed immediately during owner setup checks.
product_implication: Separate moving instances from moving the launcher. Test each owner component from its new volume.
quality_note: Direct Linux issue. It is adjacent evidence for removable-volume moves.

title: World export and deletion expected a missing source zip
observation: ATLauncher could not export, disable, or remove some downloaded worlds because it had unzipped them and then expected the original zip to remain.
product_implication: Keep world saves separate from their download artifacts. Owner metadata can point to a file that no longer represents live data.
quality_note: Owner issue with a detailed content-lifecycle explanation.

title: Large ATLauncher export omitted rate-limited mods
observation: A large instance export hit Modrinth rate limits and appeared to miss mods.
product_implication: Compare the export manifest with the live instance and test import. Do not delete local mods after an incomplete export.
quality_note: Direct issue with a concrete owner API failure.

title: Reinstall showed duplicate entries for one instance
observation: ATLauncher showed two entries for one reinstalled instance. Deleting one entry removed the shared folder while the other entry remained until restart.
product_implication: Resolve duplicate owner records to physical identity before deletion. Two rows can point to one directory.
quality_note: Direct report with a reproducible identity collision.

title: ATLauncher could not import a NeoForge instance
observation: A zipped NeoForge instance failed owner import because the loader identifier was not understood.
product_implication: Test the exact loader and owner version before treating an export as recoverable.
quality_note: Direct issue with owner import logs.

title: Imported instance lost VM and memory settings
observation: A user exported an instance with custom VM and memory settings, but ATLauncher ignored those settings on import.
product_implication: Compare launch configuration after restore. A playable file set can still lose machine-specific settings.
quality_note: Direct report with export and import verification steps.

title: ATLauncher export reported a read-only filesystem
observation: A user could write with other tools but ATLauncher failed to create an export and reported the filesystem as read-only.
product_implication: Use owner completion status and verify the archive file. General filesystem writability is not enough.
quality_note: Direct report with the owner exception path.

title: Rate limiting required repeated instance creation attempts
observation: Minecraft asset requests were rate-limited during instance creation. ATLauncher kept already downloaded files, and the user completed the instance after several retries.
product_implication: Protect partial downloads that the owner can resume. Do not treat every incomplete instance as discardable staging.
quality_note: Direct report with a successful resume counterexample.

title: Imported MultiMC instance failed from exported null commands
observation: An ATLauncher instance exported in MultiMC format imported on another system but failed until null command settings were cleared.
product_implication: A post-move check must launch the imported instance and inspect owner command settings.
quality_note: Direct cross-system export and import report.

title: ATLauncher export produced a profile Prism could not import
observation: A user reported that ATLauncher's MultiMC export could not be imported by Prism Launcher.
product_implication: Do not assume format labels guarantee cross-launcher recovery. Test the intended destination owner.
quality_note: Direct owner issue with a cross-launcher counterexample.

title: itch could not link a manual download to its library
observation: A user downloaded files from an external provider but the itch app had no way to connect those files to the owned game entry.
product_implication: Treat unregistered payload as recoverable. Offer owner link or import before recommending another download or deletion.
quality_note: Direct issue with a current missing owner workflow.

title: itch duplicated installed games after losing status
observation: After rapid installs, some itch buttons still said Install and created redundant folders with numeric suffixes instead of recognizing existing files.
product_implication: Match owner IDs and file roots before deleting duplicates. Keep the copy that the owner can launch and verify exclusive bytes.
quality_note: Direct report with a repeatable high-concurrency condition.

title: itch rejected a removable SSD install location
observation: A user could add a location on the system drive but not a removable SSD even though the user could write to it.
product_implication: Probe owner registration and actual write access separately before moving payload.
quality_note: Direct report with owner logs and a removable-volume comparison.

title: HTML game could not be installed for offline play
observation: A browser-playable itch game had no compatible app download, so the user could not install it for offline use while another HTML game worked.
product_implication: Offline availability is per build. Do not promise redownload or offline recovery from a store listing alone.
quality_note: Direct counterexample comparing two HTML games.

title: itch scan did not recognize website downloads
observation: A user downloaded games from the itch website during a client login problem and later could not make the client recognize them.
product_implication: Do not treat unregistered website downloads as junk. Preserve them until owner import support or a checksum match exists.
quality_note: Direct first-person recovery question.

title: itch setup blocked DRM-free games while offline
observation: A user said DRM-free game files could run offline directly, but itch app setup timed out before the launcher exposed them.
product_implication: Offer the direct executable as a recovery path when safe. Distinguish launcher availability from payload availability.
quality_note: Direct report with a useful counterexample between direct and owner launch.

title: itch macOS install hung across a symlinked volume
observation: A macOS user's Applications folder was a symlink to a read-only location on another volume. itch downloaded the app and then hung while moving it into place.
product_implication: Check target-volume writability and cross-volume move semantics before cleanup. Preserve the completed download until retry succeeds.
quality_note: Direct macOS report with path and volume conditions.

title: itch staging rename failed with access denied
observation: itch setup downloaded a ready version but could not rename the staging folder into its final location because access was denied.
product_implication: Keep ready staging when the final move alone failed. It may save a full redownload after permissions repair.
quality_note: Direct issue with the exact failing owner operation.

title: Interrupted itch install left download cache after uninstall
observation: A macOS user quit an out-of-space install, relaunched itch, and uninstalled the game, but the downloaded cache remained on disk.
product_implication: After owner uninstall, rescan staging and cache. Leftovers can be safe only after confirming the install is not resumable or wanted.
quality_note: Direct macOS reproduction with an exact operation sequence.

title: itch ignored install expansion and filled the Mac disk
observation: A macOS user started with about 12 GB free. The download completed, then installation expansion filled the disk and the client remained stuck.
product_implication: Calculate download, unpack, patch, and safety headroom separately before starting owner work.
quality_note: Direct macOS report with a measured starting free-space value.

title: itch would not register a non-system-drive install location
observation: A user installed itch on another drive but the app would not retain a game install location outside the system drive.
product_implication: Verify the owner saved the new root before copying or removing files.
quality_note: Direct owner issue. The platform is Windows, so it is adjacent evidence.

title: itch mixed download storage with install storage
observation: A user requested a separate download location because itch placed downloads inside the game install location.
product_implication: Discover download artifacts independently. Do not assume every large file under an install root is live payload.
quality_note: Direct feature request describing current owner placement.

title: itch game backup required a website download
observation: A user wanted a download-the-archive action in the app because backing up uninstalled games was easier through the website.
product_implication: Show whether an owned installer exists locally and whether it can be downloaded again. Keep offline installers distinct from installed payload.
quality_note: Direct request relayed into the owner's tracker.

title: itch scan could not map an unknown location identifier
observation: The owner issue says scanned games can carry install-location identifiers that no longer exist and proposes mapping them to a current registered location.
product_implication: Repair stale owner location IDs before treating their game folders as orphaned.
quality_note: Owner engineering issue with no user narrative, labeled as an owner fact.

title: itch tied install-location removal to game uninstall
observation: The owner issue distinguishes removing a registered install location from uninstalling its games and says active downloads should block location removal.
product_implication: Present deregistration and payload deletion as separate actions. Block both while downloads are active.
quality_note: Owner engineering issue that defines intended state boundaries.

title: itch install failure needed staging cleanup
observation: The owner issue calls for cleaning the staging directory after an install fails to queue.
product_implication: Treat this staging class as owner-confirmed cleanup only after the queue failure is terminal and no resume state remains.
quality_note: Owner engineering issue with a narrow cleanup target.

title: Removing an itch location threatened installed games
observation: A user avoided removing an install location because itch said it would uninstall the tracked games inside it, while the user wanted only to forget the location.
product_implication: Never bundle location deregistration with payload deletion in Tessera. Explain the owner's wider effect before handoff.
quality_note: Direct user report relayed through the owner's feedback channel.

title: Cancelling itch repair left files on disk
observation: The owner tracker records that cancelling a heal operation leaves files on disk.
product_implication: Mark cancelled repair output as partial. Let the owner resume or verify it before deletion.
quality_note: Concise owner engineering issue with limited context.

title: Whisky bottle disappeared after creation
observation: A macOS user created a Whisky bottle and saw it disappear from the app immediately.
product_implication: Check the filesystem and Whisky registry before calling a missing bottle orphaned or deleted.
quality_note: Direct macOS report with bottle path in logs.

title: Reinstalled Whisky could not open a surviving C drive
observation: After reinstalling Whisky, a user manually restored bottle visibility but could not open its C drive or place Steam in it.
product_implication: A re-imported bottle needs a C-drive and launch test before its source copy is removed.
quality_note: Direct macOS recovery report.

title: Game save crashed when a temporary save directory could not be deleted
observation: A game inside Whisky hung during save because it could not recursively replace a temporary save directory.
product_implication: Do not delete save-adjacent temporary directories while the game is active. They can be part of an atomic save transaction.
quality_note: Direct macOS container report with the exact save path and failing operation.

title: Steam downloads stalled inside a Whisky bottle
observation: A user reported that Steam downloads and completed installs inside Whisky stalled until Steam was exited and restarted.
product_implication: Keep owner staging while restart can resume or finalize it. Verify completion inside the container before cleanup.
quality_note: Direct issue with repeated behavior.

title: Deleting Whisky app and bottles left support files
observation: A user found that deleting the app and bottle did not remove Whisky files under Application Support and requested a complete owner removal guide.
product_implication: Show app, bottles, runtimes, logs, and support state separately. Leftover does not mean safe until ownership and recovery value are known.
quality_note: Direct macOS issue with a named leftover root.

title: Whisky created 12 GB and 4 GB logs
observation: A user found two Whisky logs at 12 GB and 4 GB while normal logs were only kilobytes.
product_implication: Detect runaway logs by growth and repetition. Keep recent diagnostic tails if a related operation failed.
quality_note: Direct report with file sizes and location.

title: Rockstar launcher missed a game on an external drive
observation: A user stored the Whisky bottle and GTA V on an external drive, but Rockstar's scan found no supported install.
product_implication: Verify every nested launcher after a move. Whisky seeing a bottle does not prove Rockstar or Epic sees the game.
quality_note: Direct macOS report spanning Whisky, Heroic, Epic, and Rockstar.

title: Direct game launch bypassed Steam cloud saves
observation: A user could launch Baldur's Gate 3 directly inside Whisky but could not access Steam cloud saves without a working Steam launch.
product_implication: A direct executable launch proves payload viability, not cloud-save recovery. Test through the account owner too.
quality_note: Direct macOS feature request with a clear launcher-bypass tradeoff.

title: Whisky bottle existed on disk but not in the app
observation: A user found a newly created bottle folder on disk while Whisky showed no bottle entry.
product_implication: Use both physical and owner views. Missing registration must trigger recovery, not folder deletion.
quality_note: Direct macOS report with contrasting app and filesystem states.

title: Manually imported Whisky bottle still could not run
observation: A fresh macOS install created bottle files without a visible owner entry. Manual import restored the row, but commands and the C drive still failed.
product_implication: Require owner command and game launch tests after bottle import before declaring recovery complete.
quality_note: Direct macOS report with a failed recovery attempt.

title: Whisky had no supported external-drive install path
observation: A Mac owner with limited internal storage said the only available way to place Whisky and bottles externally was a manual symlink.
product_implication: Do not automate external moves without an owner-supported registration path and post-remount verification.
quality_note: Direct feature request grounded in a storage constraint.

title: Whisky forgot every bottle after quit
observation: A user had to import a bottle again after every Whisky restart because the app did not retain it in the owner list.
product_implication: Include quit and relaunch in the post-move test. Immediate visibility is not enough.
quality_note: Direct macOS issue with short reproduction steps.

title: Whisky lost an external bottle after remount
observation: A user created a bottle on an external drive, unplugged and remounted the drive, and found that Whisky no longer listed the bottle.
product_implication: A missing external volume must freeze orphan detection. After remount, verify owner registration before any cleanup.
quality_note: Direct report with two remount sequences.

title: Whisky could neither retain nor import bottles
observation: A user reported that both new and imported bottles were absent from Whisky's list.
product_implication: Do not assume failed import means invalid bottle data. Preserve the folder and diagnose owner registry state.
quality_note: Direct macOS issue with owner logs.

title: External Whisky bottle disappeared on APFS and exFAT
observation: A user created bottles on an external SSD and saw them disappear from Whisky on both APFS and exFAT despite Full Disk Access.
product_implication: Do not reduce external recovery to one filesystem check. Verify owner registration, bookmarks, and remount identity.
quality_note: Direct macOS counterexample across two filesystems.

title: PlayCover users asked for separate app and data locations
observation: A user with limited Mac storage asked to place game data or both app and data on an external disk.
product_implication: Model PlayCover app payload and container data separately. A move must preserve both owner links.
quality_note: Direct macOS feature request with a specific storage constraint.

title: PlayCover uninstall left 30 GB of game data
observation: A user selected removal of associated data in PlayCover, but a 30 GB game container remained visible to a disk scanner.
product_implication: Rescan owner container paths after uninstall and show the remaining size. Owner completion does not prove all selected effects occurred.
quality_note: Direct macOS report with a measured leftover.

title: PlayCover uninstall kept the app-data container
observation: A user selected every PlayCover removal option, yet the app-data folder under Library Containers remained.
product_implication: Verify each requested owner effect by exact path. Offer leftover review after uninstall instead of claiming full removal.
quality_note: Direct macOS report with owner options and the surviving path.

title: PlayCover user needed a backup before formatting
observation: A user asked how to back up PlayCover games before formatting the computer.
product_implication: Do not assume IPA reinstall restores game state. Identify and test container-data backup separately.
quality_note: Direct recovery question with limited implementation detail.

title: PlayCover game data filled internal storage
observation: A user said large PlayCover games stored most space in application data and asked to choose both app and data locations.
product_implication: Measure the container as well as the installed app. Moving only the app may reclaim little space.
quality_note: Direct macOS request that names the large data role.

title: PlayCover app and data had no selectable storage root
observation: A user running out of Mac storage asked to choose another location for the app or its data.
product_implication: Mark external relocation unsupported until the owner exposes or verifies a stable root.
quality_note: Direct macOS feature request.

title: Internal-only PlayCover installs blocked updates
observation: A user said internal-only game storage could prevent both installation and update when the Mac lacked enough space.
product_implication: Include patch headroom and container growth in PlayCover recommendations, not only current app size.
quality_note: Direct macOS request describing the storage outcome.

title: Large PlayCover packages prompted external-drive request
observation: A user asked to install large PlayCover game packages on an external hard drive because the Mac drive was too small.
product_implication: Show owner support state and post-move test requirements before proposing external placement.
quality_note: Direct macOS request. It does not prove current external support.

title: PlayCover backup request included app and data
observation: A user requested a right-click backup that would copy both an installed app and its data to a chosen disk for transfer.
product_implication: A valid PlayCover recovery bundle must define whether app, data, keymaps, settings, entitlements, and credentials are included.
quality_note: Direct macOS feature request with a manual-copy fallback.

title: PlayCover custom storage path request
observation: A user with a full internal drive asked PlayCover to store app data on an external device.
product_implication: Keep this as an unsupported move need unless current owner behavior proves otherwise.
quality_note: Direct macOS request with no claim of existing support.

title: Steam would not adopt a one-terabyte existing library
observation: After reinstalling Steam, a user had more than one terabyte of games on an external drive but Steam kept creating a new library folder instead of using the old one.
product_implication: Preserve app manifests and owner folder structure during a move. Test owner adoption before deleting any source library.
quality_note: Direct Steam user report. Peer fixes are not treated as owner facts.

title: Moved Steam games still pointed to the old drive
observation: A user copied an external game library to a new SSD, but the games still tried to launch from the old drive.
product_implication: A byte-for-byte copy is incomplete until Steam resolves the new library and launches the game.
quality_note: Direct Steam report. Suggested peer repair steps were not used as owner facts.

title: Steam relocation affected saves and mods differently by game
observation: One user reported that most games worked after relocation, one lost progress and saves, another kept saves, and mods stopped being detected.
product_implication: Post-move tests must open each important game, load a save, and verify mods. Library-level success is too weak.
quality_note: Direct multi-game counterexample. It does not establish prevalence.

title: Drive-letter change hid Steam games after OS reinstall
observation: After an OS reinstall changed drive letters, Steam could no longer access games that remained on the external drive.
product_implication: Track stable volume identity and owner path separately. A changed mount name can look like missing payload.
quality_note: Direct Steam report on Windows, adjacent to macOS volume-name and bookmark failures.

title: Steam reinstall lost games until manifests and folders were restored
observation: A user reinstalled Steam and found that downloaded games no longer appeared even though the files remained.
product_implication: Treat Steam app manifests and userdata as owner metadata with recovery value. Game payload alone is not enough.
quality_note: Direct Steam report. Peer recovery advice provides context but is not owner documentation.

title: Epic did not restore local games after relocation or reinstall
observation: A user reported that Epic showed existing local games as missing after folder relocation, launcher reinstall, or device change and started full downloads.
product_implication: Preserve Epic manifests and use owner verification before source deletion. Existing payload without registration is recoverable state.
quality_note: Direct report on Epic's first-party forum with an Epic staff acknowledgement.

title: Epic move required game files and manifests
observation: Users reported that copying a large Epic library alone left the launcher demanding an empty folder, while restoring matching manifest state let some installs reappear.
product_implication: Treat manifest state as part of the move. Test every title because forum reports include mixed outcomes.
quality_note: Long first-party forum thread with several firsthand attempts. Peer methods are not official support.

title: Epic launcher could not find an engine on an external drive
observation: A user put a large Epic-managed engine on an external drive, but the launcher could not find or select it.
product_implication: Owner recognition must be tested after external moves even when the executable can run directly.
quality_note: Direct first-party forum report. It concerns an engine payload, adjacent to game payloads.

title: GOG cloud restored saves the user wanted deleted
observation: A user deleted local saves, then GOG Galaxy restored years of old saves from the cloud on a new computer.
product_implication: Cloud state can undo local cleanup. Show remote and local generations and let the owner resolve the intended state first.
quality_note: Direct GOG forum report. Peer guidance is not treated as owner documentation.

title: Moving GOG games required scan and import
observation: Users described moving game folders, reinstalling Galaxy, and importing the new location. The thread also warns users to protect saves because outcomes differ.
product_implication: Use owner import and a per-game save test before deleting the old copy.
quality_note: Direct GOG forum thread with multiple firsthand outcomes.

title: Battle.net uninstall removed years of screenshots
observation: A player uninstalled World of Warcraft to free space and then found years of screenshots gone, while a Classic uninstall had left different content behind.
product_implication: Inventory screenshots, addons, and settings per game edition before owner uninstall. Similar owner actions can have different effects.
quality_note: Direct first-person data-loss report. Replies note that the forum no longer had staff support.

title: Moving Battle.net files made the game appear uninstalled
observation: A user moved Blizzard files to another drive and Battle.net then reported that the game was not installed.
product_implication: Move through owner controls where possible and verify registration after restart. A raw folder move can sever owner state.
quality_note: Direct Blizzard forum report with an owner-support reply.

title: WoW backup preserved addons and settings separately from payload
observation: Players preparing for a disk wipe separated the redownloadable game from Interface and WTF folders that hold addons, settings, and macros, and noted that Battle.net may need to be pointed to the copied game.
product_implication: Protect Interface, WTF, screenshots, and owner location state before removing or moving the game payload.
quality_note: Direct Blizzard forum thread with concrete backup categories. Peer guidance is not official policy.
